chunks.heading: What is The Power of Art
chunks.notes: Opens with the cave-art origin image and a claim about artists ("charcoal-smeared palms") before cataloguing painters, musicians, and "unknown architects."

chunks.heading: What is The Power of Art
chunks.notes: Repeats the "There would be no X without Y" formula across three lineage chains, closing with the literal "torch passed hand to hand."

chunks.heading: What is The Power of Art
chunks.notes: Continues the anaphoric lineage chains and lands on the aphoristic summary "Every artist is both a descendant and an ancestor."

chunks.heading: What is The Power of Art
chunks.notes: Pivots to warning ("It will dim slowly, quietly, almost politely") and then immediately re-narrates the image in abstract terms via the literal phrase "invisible architecture of a culture."

chunks.heading: What is The Power of Art
chunks.notes: Turns on the rhetorical question "whether we can afford not to" and closes on the tender/melancholy image of the child who stopped drawing.

chunks.heading: What is The Power of Art
chunks.notes: Repeats "Every artist... Every masterpiece..." before pivoting on "But it doesn't have to be that way" into the concrete "We can choose to..." action triad.

chunks.heading: What is The Power of Art
chunks.notes: Closes by calling back to the ancestor image from chunk 1 and ends on the watching/listening pairing "The future is watching. The next artist is listening."
